reason: The Egyptian magicians and wise men (חַרְטֻמֵּי מִצְרַיִם וְחַכָּמֶיהָ) are portrayed as inadequate and incapable. The text explicitly states 'וְאֵין־ פּוֹתֵר אוֹתָם לְפַרְעֹה' (and there is none who can interpret them for Pharaoh), showing these elite officials unable to fulfill their primary function. This failure is further emphasized by Joseph's subsequent success in interpreting the dreams—a feat that eluded all of Egypt's supposed experts. The narrative structure inherently portrays the elite as incompetent, with their incapacity contrasted dramatically against an enslaved Hebrew youth's superior wisdom.
